name: Hearty Lentil French Onion Soup With Melty Gruyère

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, plus more for bread
kosher salt, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice the yellow onions. Grate the Gruyère cheese.
instructions.secondary_message:
8 medium yellow onions
8 oz Gruyère cheese

instructions.primary_message: In a large Dutch oven, melt butter over medium-high heat until foaming. Add onions, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are softened, 6 to 8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring frequently and scraping bottom of pot as needed, until onions are sweet and deeply caramelized, 45 minutes to 1 hour. If browned onion juices on bottom of pot threaten to burn, add 1 tablespoon water, scrape up browned bits, and continue cooking.
Add sherry, scraping up any browned bits, and cook over medium until alcohol is mostly evaporated, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add stock or broth, lentils, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender but hold their shape, 25 to 30 minutes.
Remove and discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in apple cider vinegar. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Preheat broiler and adjust oven rack to about 6 inches from heat source. Lightly butter toasted French bread slices, and rub with garlic clove until fragrant.
Ladle soup evenly into 4 broiler-safe bowls. Top each bowl with 2 slices of bread, overlapping slightly. Sprinkle each bowl evenly with 1/2 cup (2 ounces) Gruyère cheese.
Place bowls on a rimmed baking sheet. Broil until cheese is melted and browned in spots, about 3 to 4 minutes. Garnish with thyme leaves, and serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: Lentil French onion soup recipe, French onion soup

description: Lentil soup meets French onion soup in this hearty winter mashup with deeply caramelized onions and molten Gruyère cheese.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 fresh thyme sprigs, plus thyme leaves for garnish

Optional substitutions: homemade beef stock → low-sodium chicken stock

Notes: Yellow onions are the best all-purpose choice for this soup, but a mix of yellow, sweet (e.g., Vidalia), and red onions, along with shallots, produces an even more complex flavor.

Make-ahead and storage: The soup base can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days before assembling and broiling the soup to serve.
author: Leah Colins
